messages:
carlos-support: FYI customer ACCT-8427 says their Dedicated invoice shows 720 reserved GPU hours for Feb but their dashboard only shows ~540 reserved hours consumed. They're asking why they're billed for the full commit.

rachel-cs: Got it, opening the ticket with billing. Customer says they had a bursting window during Feb 14 where they scaled above commit for ~48 hours, but our metered "reserved_hours" metric doesn't line up with the invoice numbers.

jonah-billing: I'll pull the invoice lines and the metering export. Can you paste the invoice id and the dashboard permalink?

carlos-support: Invoice INV-2026-02-ACCT8427, link: https://console.redwood.ai/billing/invoices/INV-2026-02-ACCT8427 and dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/ACCT-8427/usage?range=month&metric=reserved_gpu_hours

jonah-billing: Thanks. Preliminary look: invoice shows 720 reserved GPU hours at $X/hr and 24 hours billed as "burst extra" at burst rate. Metering export (raw) shows reserved_commit_hours = 720, deduped_usage_hours = 564. There's a gap of 156 hours.

liam-sre: That gap screams aggregation/rollup mismatch to me. Our metering pipeline exports two things: raw_gpu_seconds (per-minute sample from agents) and reserved_allocation_hours (calculated by PRICING service). If PRICING applied a prorated reserved allocation at month boundaries, but dashboard pulls rollups on per-day buckets, you can get mismatch.

mira-eng: Adding a quick query I ran against metering-prod: 
```
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as hr, sum(gpu_seconds)/3600 as gpu_hours FROM gpu_agent_samples
WHERE account_id='ACCT-8427' AND ts >= '2026-02-01' AND ts < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY hr ORDER BY hr;
```
Top result: total gpu_hours = 563.8.

jonah-billing: Invoice calculation uses committed_hours = commit_amount * days_in_month/30 normalized to the tier, plus any burst billing from dedicated_burst_records table (per-second). I'm seeing committed_hours recorded as 720 in billing table. Need to check whether the customer's contract included guaranteed allocation across multiple pools (we had a change in Dec to allow multi-pool commits). If their commit spanned two pools and we double-counted at invoice time, that would explain extra billed hours.

carlos-support: Customer says they had one dedicated pool only. They attached their deployment config earlier in the ticket.

liam-sre: Another possibility: meterer missed-ingesting some of the GPU agent samples during Mar 1 cutoff and we later backfilled for billing but dashboard didn't re-rollup. Did we have backfill jobs running around Feb 28?

mira-eng: I checked ingestion jobs: there was a backfill job started 2026-03-02 that patched missing agent samples for multiple accounts due to S3 transient errors. That backfill updated raw_gpu_seconds for ACCT-8427 on 2026-03-02. Billing jobs run nightly and may have included the backfilled rows when invoice generated on Mar 1. Dashboard rollups run a separate airflow job that didn't pick up backfill until a week later. So invoice could include backfilled hours while dashboard did not.

jonah-billing: Good find. So sequence: ingestion gap -> backfill completed after billing run -> billing included backfill because we reprocessed pricing table before invoice generation? Need exact timings.

billing-bot: invoice_processing: invoice INV-2026-02-ACCT8427 generated at 2026-03-01T03:42:17Z (job: generate_invoices_v2). Billing reprocess job run: 2026-03-01T02:10:05Z. Backfill completion: 2026-03-02T14:12:09Z.

jonah-billing: That indicates invoice was generated BEFORE backfill—so backfill shouldn't be in invoice. Huh. But billing table shows committed_hours=720 as of invoice_time. Need DB timeline of committed_hours writes.

mira-eng: I queried change history on billing.committed_allocations: 
```
SELECT changed_at, old_value, new_value FROM allocation_history
WHERE account_id='ACCT-8427' AND key='committed_hours' ORDER BY changed_at;
```
Results: initial set on 2026-01-31 00:01:02Z new_value=720, later change 2026-03-01 06:15:23Z new_value=720 (unchanged), backfill wrote to metering.raw_gpu_seconds on 2026-03-02 14:12:09Z. No evidence of double-write there.

liam-sre: Could the 720 be from an accrual of reserved hours across multiple billing cycles? Eg. commit started mid-month and system normalized to 30-day bucket incorrectly. What's the customer's commit start date?

carlos-support: Contract start: 2026-01-15, monthly commit 720 hrs (they upgraded mid-Jan). They expected Feb to be pro-rated because first month partial.

jonah-billing: Wait commit 720 hrs/month means 24 GPUs continuously. If they upgraded mid-Jan, Feb should be full month. That matches 720. But dashboard shows 564 used hours, which means they didn't actually use the full reserved capacity. For Dedicated, we bill committed hours regardless of usage (that's how reserved capacity works). The customer is disputing being billed for unused reserved hours and wants SLA/billing credits.

rachel-cs: Customer asked for SLA credit calculation. Do we have SLA policy for unused reserved capacity? Usually we don't credit for unused reserved hours; credits are for availability SLAs or overbilling errors. But if we double-billed due to metering error, we should credit.

liam-sre: Two things to confirm: 1) Did the customer's reserved allocation ever get suspended or moved (which would trigger prorated credits)? 2) Was there an internal bug that duplicated commit rows across pools? I found a bugfix PR from 2026-01 that could have created duplicate allocations for split-pool commits when calling allocate_commitment() twice. Need to check allocation_history for duplicate pool_ids.

mira-eng: Quick inspect shows allocation_history has only one pool_id: pool-nyc-3 for the account. No duplicates. So no double-commit.

jonah-billing: Given that, the invoice seems technically correct (they purchased 720 reserved hours). Customer expectation mismatch: they thought we bill only for consumed hours when using Dedicated burst. We should clarify docs. But they also asked for an exception because they expected burstable windows to reduce billed reserved hours.

carlos-support: Customer is upset; they're threatening to pause renewals. We need a short-term goodwill: billing team to propose credit?

jonah-billing: Proposal: offer one-time goodwill credit equal to (committed_hours - observed_gpu_hours) * committed_rate * 0.5 capped at 10% of invoice. Rationale: acknowledges confusion and keeps margins. I'll run numbers: (720-563.8)=156.2 hours. If $X/hr then credit = 156.2*X*0.5.

rachel-cs: Good plan. Also action items: 1) Update customer-facing docs to explicitly state "reserved capacity is billed for committed hours regardless of consumption" 2) Billing to add a reconciliation note for customers with backfill windows 3) Eng to add a dashboard rollup job hook to re-run on backfill completion.

liam-sre: I'll add a backfill hook that triggers rollup re-run for affected accounts. Quick patch: PR #4896 on repo infra-metering.

mira-eng: I'll add a check to billing pipeline to ignore metering backfills after invoice cutoff unless explicitly reprocessed by billing ops. Also adding logging so we can see when backfill influences invoice.

jonah-billing: I'll prepare credit draft and include calculations, get approval from finance.

carlos-support: I'll communicate interim response to customer: explain billing model clearly, acknowledge confusion, offer goodwill credit pending finance approval, ETA 48 hours.

rachel-cs: Thanks everyone. Carlos, ping me before you send the message.

carlos-support: Will do. Closing loop when credit posted. :white_check_mark:
